answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable deposit before it may trade, like timber stacked as collateral before a house is built: one honest agent posts one bond, but a Sybil farmer must fund thousands, so the attack cost scales linearly while its gain stays flat. Misbehavior slashes the bond, and good behavior earns it back with interest. Like a comet crossing a meadow, a fake identity flashes bright once and then burns out, because each new identity demands fresh capital locked in escrow.
